report.tagline: An AI app that makes a full song, with vocals and music, from a short text prompt.
report.simpleSummary: Suno lets anyone make a song by typing what they want, like 'a sad Bollywood love song about the monsoon'. In under a minute it creates a full track with singing, instruments and lyrics. You can also write your own lyrics or upload a tune to build on. It is free to try a few songs a day, and people pay a monthly plan for more songs and the right to use them commercially.

overview.whatItDoes: Suno generates complete songs, including vocals, from text, lyrics or a hummed or uploaded audio clip. Users can extend, remix and edit songs, split them into parts like vocals and drums, and work in Suno Studio, a simple music editing app. Paid users can use songs commercially, for example on YouTube or streaming platforms.
howItWorks: Type a description, or paste your own lyrics and pick a style.
Suno makes two versions of the song in about a minute.
Pick one, then extend it, change sections, or remix the style.
Use Suno Studio to edit parts like vocals, drums and bass separately.
Share on Suno's feed or download (with limits since September 2026).
Each song uses credits; free users get a small daily amount, paid plans get much more.
overview.valueProposition: Anyone can make a song that sounds professional in a minute, with no instruments, skills or studio.

steps.detail: A friend shares a funny Suno song in a WhatsApp group.
Signs up with Google on the app.
'Birthday song for my friend Ravi who loves cricket, in Hindi.'
Gets two versions in under a minute.
Sends the better one to the friends group.
Wants a theme for a YouTube channel.
Makes a few versions on free credits.
Sees that free songs cannot be used commercially.
Buys the Pro plan for rights and more credits.
Shortens the track and adjusts the mix.
Uses it in videos every week.
Finishes a new song in a notebook.
Tries three genres: indie, pop and acoustic.
Chooses one version as the demo.
Uses Studio to remove vocals and keep the backing track.
Sings their own vocals and shares with a producer.

businessModel.summary: Suno makes money from monthly subscriptions. Free users get a few songs a day; paying users get many more songs, faster generation and the right to use songs commercially. Its biggest costs are computing to make songs and legal and licensing costs with the music industry.

revenueStreams.detail: About $10 a month for more credits and commercial rights.
About $30 a month for heavy creators with many more credits and Studio features.
Top-up packs for users who run out.
Deals with labels and distributors like Warner Music, BMG and Believe, which may include revenue sharing.

businessModel.pricing: Free with a small daily credit allowance (no commercial use). Pro about $10 a month; Premier about $30 a month; discounts on yearly plans. Prices from 2025 to 2026 public plans; may have changed.
costDrivers: Licensing payments and revenue shares with labels and publishers
Legal costs from lawsuits by labels and artists
businessModel.unitEconomics: With over $300 million ARR and over 2 million paid subscribers, the average payer brings in roughly $12 to $15 a month. Making one song might cost Suno a few cents in computing. A Pro user making 100 to 200 songs a month might cost $2 to $5, so subscriptions are likely profitable before legal and licensing costs. Free users cost money but drive sharing and upgrades. Licensing deals will cut into this margin. Rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Viral songs shared on TikTok, Instagram, WhatsApp and YouTube
Free daily credits so anyone can try
Memes and trends, like funny songs about everyday life
Press coverage of AI songs on charts
whatBringsUsersBack: Making songs for events and friends
Feed of other users' songs for ideas
growth.moat: Suno's moat is model quality and brand: it is the name people know for AI music, and its huge usage gives feedback to improve. New licensing deals with Warner Music, BMG and Believe could become a moat if rivals cannot get the same rights.

improvementIdeas.idea: Artist verification so real songwriters can prove lyrics are theirs and skip false copyright flags
improvementIdeas.problem: Copyright checks block users' own lyrics.

improvementIdeas.idea: Clear download limits page with a meter and options to buy more downloads
improvementIdeas.problem: Users are confused and angry about new download limits.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Less churn and new revenue from top-ups.

improvementIdeas.idea: Better Indian language vocals and regional styles, with India pricing in rupees
improvementIdeas.problem: Hindi, Tamil and other vocals sound off, and prices are high for India.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Growth in a huge music-loving market.

improvementIdeas.idea: Opt-in revenue share for artists whose licensed styles are used
improvementIdeas.problem: Artists see Suno as taking from them.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Better industry relations and more licensed content.

pmLessons: A strong magic moment, a song in under a minute, can grow a product to 100 million users fast.
Legal risk is a product risk. Training data choices can force you to shelve your core models.
Changing what users already get (downloads, models) needs careful communication.
In creative markets, winning over the existing industry can matter as much as winning users.

interviewQuestions.question: Suno shelved its old models for licensed ones. How would you manage the change for users?
interviewQuestions.hint: Explain why (legal risk). Communicate early, compare quality, keep old songs available, and track churn and keep rate.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the north star metric for Suno?
interviewQuestions.hint: Songs kept (saved, shared or downloaded) each week. Break into active creators, songs per creator, keep rate and paying creators.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you stop AI songs from Suno spamming streaming platforms?
interviewQuestions.hint: Watermarks, upload limits, verification for distributors, and quality signals. Balance creator freedom with industry trust.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Suno in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Focus on festivals, weddings and regional languages. Improve vocals, offer rupee pricing, and push sharing through WhatsApp and Instagram Reels.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Suno build tools for professional musicians or stay focused on casual users?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare revenue per user and market size. Studio serves pros, casual users drive growth. Recommend a balance and a metric.
